title: IAM API feature gating: explicit config vs OpenFeature dual path
answers: How do I gate a new IAM API/route behind a feature flag?
Why does register.go call featureEnabled instead of ofClient.Boolean directly?
How does explicit startup IAM config interact with OpenFeature flags?
body: Every IAM API gate check must go through IdentityAccessManagementAPIBuilder.featureEnabled(ctx, flagKey, func(Features) bool) in pkg/registry/apis/iam/register.go, not ofClient.Boolean directly. It returns the explicit Features value if b.features != nil, otherwise falls back to the OpenFeature flag. REST connectors that need the same per-request gate (e.g. TeamMembersREST, UserTeamREST) follow the same nil-checked-pointer pattern: a `*bool` field set only via a `...WithFeature` constructor, checked before falling back to ofClient.Boolean. Any new gated API/route must add both paths to stay consistent with standalone (explicit-config) and embedded (OpenFeature) deployments.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/iam/register.go and any REST handler in pkg/registry/apis/iam/{team,user}/ that gates behavior by an IAM feature flag
